tools: the project's Makefile with its sbt launcher (./sbt, sbt 1.9.6 from project/build.properties); Linux x86_64 with GNU make, gcc/g++, cmake (reference build: make 4.3, gcc 11.5.0, cmake 3.22.2, Amazon Linux 2023)
notes: Build = the Makefile's default target (snappy = native + ./sbt package): native clones google/snappy 1.1.10 and downloads bitshuffle 0.3.4 (versions from src/main/resources/org/xerial/snappy/VERSION), compiles them with SnappyNative.cpp/BitShuffleNative.cpp (Linux-x86_64 flags of Makefile.common, -static-libgcc -static-libstdc++), strips the library and copies it to src/main/resources/org/xerial/snappy/native/Linux/x86_64/libsnappyjava.so; sbt package then compiles the Java sources (javac --release 8) and packages them with src/main/resources, which also hold the 25 prebuilt native libraries for the other platforms committed at this commit. Overwriting the tracked Linux/x86_64 library makes the work tree dirty, so sbt-dynver appends the build time to the version (1.1.10.3-17-49d70017-<yyyyMMdd-HHmm>-SNAPSHOT); the second command copies the newest such jar to the name the fixture uses, which has no time in it (snappy-java-1.1.10.3-17-49d70017-SNAPSHOT.jar); the fixture's jar is the build's jar with the two version lines of its MANIFEST (Specification-Version, Implementation-Version) written without the build time; every other entry is byte-identical, so classes_sha256 is the build's. The classes_sha256 covers the 40 classes, not the native library (reference Linux/x86_64 libsnappyjava.so sha256 eae07e2eb21b1a1840b103ff036933d7f13b00a98c0bda4cc075bb7968ed81d2). snappy-java has no runtime dependencies. Fixed: snappy-java 1.1.10.4.
